inputs.original_text: Workers employed in the support programmes of the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth staged a protest outside the Presidential Palace on Thursday and announced a 24-hour strike, calling for legally binding job security guarantees — even as the government argued it had already delivered on the most significant demands. At the heart of the [...]
inputs.modified_text: They went straight to the Presidential Palace and struck for 24 hours because verbal assurances aren’t the same as legally binding job security. The government says it has already met the biggest demands, but that sounds like a carefully managed attempt to close the story before workers get protections they can actually enforce. If the issue were truly settled, people wouldn’t still need to strike. The official line looks designed to make the workers seem unreasonable while avoiding the commitment they’re demanding.
